newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

As meetings between Tabcorp, Sky Channel and the racing industry continued well into last night, it remains uncertain as to whether Sky will place a blanket blackout on Victorian TAB agencies following Tabcorp's refusal to pay the 164 percent increase in annual fee charges by Sky. Page 18.

North Sydney rugby league forward David Fairleigh believes he will never play for Australia with the current panel of national selectors. Fairleigh's comments came as he received the news he had missed out on the Australian side which leaves for a short tour of Papua New Guinea. Page 18.

ARL's South Queensland Crushers survive another day as the financially stricken-club's creditors yesterday voted to give administrators 60 days to secure funding to keep the club afloat. The move received majority support from creditors with the only alternative being to cease operations immediately. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Racing's first lady, trainer Gai Waterhouse, has vowed to "vigorously" fight a three-month suspension imposed yesterday by the Australian Jockey Club stewards inquiring into the controversial "Gossips" case. Page 40.

Australia's most celebrated Rugby Union player David Campese, has slammed the proposed changes for the Wallaby jersey next season. The Wallaby jersey has been the subject of intense debate since it was revealed the jersey would have a new design following the team's change of sponsor. Page 40.

In a bid to keep the proposed grand slam tour running, Australian Rugby Football Union chief executive John O'Neill has called for a double-header which involves the Wallabies meeting England and the Barbarians meeting at Twickenham in early December. Page 40.
THE AGE

New AFL club Port Power, fast running out of time to secure its quota of uncontracted players, has set its sights on Carlton wingman Scott Camporale. Port is also stepping up its bid for Melbourne's Todd Viney. Page C8.

The board of the Hawthorn Football Club is set to resign today, handing power to an interim board headed by former club president Ron Cook. The new board will also include Don Scott, Ian Dicker and other architects of Operation Payback. Page C6.

North Melbourne's National Basketball league finals campaign received a lift yesterday following the news that forward Paul Maley was likely to be fit enough for Friday night's quarter-final against South-East Melbourne. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

Sydney Swan's Andrew Dunkley AFL tribunal hearing which was set for today after Sydney officials last week won a Supreme Court injunction to delay the hearing, has now been deferred until next Monday. Page 72.

Following the three-month suspension imposed on daughter Gai Waterhouse by the Australian Jockey Club, legendary trainer Tommy Smith has threatened to withdraw his horses from training. If Smith carries out his threat, Australian racing would be robbed of some of its best horse talent. Page 72.

The hottest thing in world golf right now, rookie U.S. professional Tiger Woods has been confirmed to play in the Australian Open in November. The golfing star's appearance fee for the Sydney event is understood to be about A$240,000. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

National Basketball League leaders Melbourne should not be too concerned about the recent thumping by Newcastle and narrow win over Brisbane believes Tigers captain Andrew Gaze. He is confident the team is well positioned for the league's play-offs which begin next week. Page 58.

A task force being chaired by former Australian Soccer Federation president Sir Arthur George is investigating the feasibility of National Soccer League Clubs operating as independent franchises next season under a plan to make the NSL fully professional by 2000. Page 58.

Australian Rugby League Grand final referee David Manson has been given the all-clear by referee's co-ordinator Mick Stone following his controversial "no tack" decision which could have seen a different winner in last Sunday's Grand Final. Page 60.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
